author: t. l. madrid
title: Central Arkansas extends contract of men's basketball coach John Shulman through 2030
text:
The University of Central Arkansas announced on Mar. 11 that men’s basketball head coach John Shulman has signed a contract extension, keeping him with the Bears through the 2029-2030 season.
The extension follows a successful season for the Bears, who finished with a 22-12 overall record and a 15-3 mark in ASUN Conference play. The team advanced to the ASUN Championship Finals after winning two games in the conference tournament.
Matt Whiting, Director of Athletics at Central Arkansas, said, “Coach Shulman has infused great energy into our men’s basketball program and taken our program to new heights in a very short amount of time. He and his staff have instilled a strong culture and set a new standard for men’s basketball at Central Arkansas. With the continued investment that we are making by opting into the house settlement terms and this new era of Division I athletics, as well as the plans for a new on-campus arena. I am excited about the future of Central Arkansas Basketball and proud to have Coach Shulman leading our program.”
In his second year as head coach, Shulman led the Bears to their most successful season since joining NCAA Division I. The team achieved program-best marks for overall wins, conference wins, longest winning streak, and highest finish in conference standings. They also reached the conference championship game for the first time.
The turnaround was significant compared to Shulman’s first season when the Bears finished 4-14 in ASUN play and placed tenth in the standings. This year, they improved to a first-place finish with their first regular-season conference title at this level. As a result, Shulman was named ASUN Coach of the Year.
During the season, Central Arkansas had an 11-game winning streak in conference play and won 15 out of its last 17 games. The team’s only losses against conference opponents came in overtime on away courts. Offensively, they averaged 83.6 points per game while allowing just 74.6 points defensively—both ranking second among ASUN teams—and led the league with a +9 scoring margin.
At home in Farris Center, Central Arkansas posted a dominant 15-1 record with their only loss coming in overtime.
“We came out to Conway and Central Arkansas to do something special. We got close,” said Coach Shulman. “We have unfinished business! We got a lot of work to do and we are excited about the future. UCA basketball is just getting started. I want to thank Dr. Davis and Matt Whiting for believing in our vision. Time to get back to work.”
With Shulman’s contract extended and much of its young roster returning next season, Central Arkansas aims to build on this year’s achievements as it prepares for future campaigns.
